cards.name: ExportOptionsAVIF
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsAVIF
cards.summary: Option set for Document.exportFile with ExportType.AVIF: writes the artwork as an AVIF raster, lossless by default or lossy with imageQuality 0-63, with optional alpha channel, ICC profile, XMP metadata, an anti-aliasing mode and a PPI that sets the pixel size.
use_for: small, high-quality web hero images rendered from vector art
transparent AVIF stickers and icons for modern websites
batch export of artwork to AVIF in a site build script
avoid: destinations that cannot decode AVIF (older email clients, some CMS and social uploaders): use ExportOptionsPNG24 or ExportOptionsJPEG
exporting many artboards at several sizes in one call: use Document.exportForScreens with ExportForScreensOptionsAVIF
cards.how: Create with new ExportOptionsAVIF(), set its properties, and pass it as the third argument of app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.AVIF, options). It is a plain option object, not attached to the document.

key_members.name: losslessCompression
key_members.use: true (default) = lossless; set false to make imageQuality take effect

key_members.name: imageQuality
key_members.use: lossy quality on a 0-63 scale, default 63 (top of the scale); ignored while losslessCompression is true

key_members.name: PPI
key_members.use: output resolution in pixels per inch, default 72; this sets the pixel size

key_members.name: matteColor
key_members.use: RGBColor painted behind the art when isTransparent is false

key_members.name: embedICCProfile
key_members.use: embed the document ICC profile (default false)

gotchas: imageQuality runs 0-63, not 0-100 like ExportOptionsWebP; the harvested default 63 is the top of the scale.
imageQuality does nothing until losslessCompression is set to false.
There is no horizontalScale/verticalScale here (unlike the legacy JPEG/PNG classes): pixel size comes from PPI, so set 144 or 300 for crisp output.
matteColor must be an RGBColor object and is only used when isTransparent is false.
(unverified) Whether the export is cropped to the active artboard or to the artwork bounds: test on a document with art outside the artboard.
(unverified) Which end of the 0-63 imageQuality scale is best quality; compare file sizes at 20 and 60 before batch use.

review.changes: imageQuality key member no longer asserts that 63 is the best quality (the harvest gives only the 0-63 range and the default); added an unverified gotcha about the scale direction

cards.name: ExportOptionsGIF
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsGIF
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.GIF, the legacy Save-for-Web style GIF writer: a 2-256 colour palette, colour-reduction and dither methods, web-snap, lossy compression, 1-bit transparency, interlacing, matte colour and scale percentages that set the pixel size.
use_for: flat-colour web badges and buttons with few colours
legacy email banners that must be GIF
small transparent icons where PNG is not accepted
avoid: photos, gradients and soft shadows: banding and dither noise; use ExportOptionsJPEG or ExportOptionsPNG24
anti-aliased edges over unknown backgrounds: GIF transparency is on/off, so edges fringe against matteColor; use ExportOptionsPNG24
cards.how: new ExportOptionsGIF(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.GIF, options). Resolution is set through horizontalScale/verticalScale as a percentage of 72 ppi.

key_members.name: colorCount
key_members.use: palette size 2-256, default 128; the main file-size lever

key_members.name: webSnap
key_members.use: 0-100: how far palette colours are snapped to the web palette

key_members.name: matte
key_members.use: blend edges / fill background with matteColor (default true)

key_members.name: matteColor
key_members.use: RGBColor used for matting, white by default

key_members.name: horizontalScale
key_members.use: percent of 72 ppi; 200 doubles the pixel width

key_members.name: verticalScale
key_members.use: percent of 72 ppi for the height

key_members.name: artBoardClipping
key_members.use: clip to the artboard instead of the art bounds (default false)

key_members.name: saveAsHTML
key_members.use: also write an HTML file (keep false)

gotchas: Pixel size = artwork size in points x horizontalScale/100 (72 ppi base); set both scales for 2x assets.
artBoardClipping defaults to false, so the image is cropped to the art's bounding box; set it true and pick the artboard with doc.artboards.setActiveArtboardIndex(i) first.
Transparency is 1-bit: anti-aliased edge pixels are blended into matteColor (white by default); match it to the page the GIF will sit on.
saveAsHTML writes an extra HTML file next to the image; keep it false in pipelines.

cards.name: ExportOptionsJPEG
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsJPEG
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.JPEG, the legacy Save-for-Web style JPEG writer: quality 0-100, optimized encoding, blur 0-2, matte colour behind transparent areas, scale percentages that set the pixel size, anti-aliasing and artboard clipping. The class has no colour-space or ppi setting.
use_for: web and social JPEG previews of vector layouts
client proof images of an artboard
thumbnails for a catalogue or contact sheet
avoid: art that needs transparency: JPEG has none and transparent areas take matteColor; use ExportOptionsPNG24
print rasters: no CMYK or ppi setting here; use ExportOptionsTIFF or PDFSaveOptions
logos and flat colour with hard edges where JPEG artifacts show; use ExportOptionsPNG24 or ExportOptionsPNG8
cards.how: new ExportOptionsJPEG(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.JPEG, options).

key_members.name: qualitySetting
key_members.use: JPEG quality 0-100; harvested default is only 30

key_members.name: blurAmount
key_members.use: 0-2 blur applied before compression; keep 0 for crisp art

key_members.name: matte
key_members.use: fill transparent areas with matteColor (default true)

key_members.name: matteColor
key_members.use: RGBColor behind transparent areas, white by default

key_members.name: verticalScale
key_members.use: percent of 72 ppi for the height, same range

key_members.name: artBoardClipping
key_members.use: clip to the artboard instead of the art bounds (default false)

key_members.name: saveAsHTML
key_members.use: also write an HTML file (keep false)

gotchas: qualitySetting defaults to 30 (low quality); always set it, 80-100 for deliverables.
Pixel size comes from the scale percentages (72 ppi base); the harvested maximum 776.19% (about 559 ppi) caps large exports, so use ExportOptionsTIFF (up to 2400 ppi) for big rasters.
artBoardClipping defaults to false: output is cropped to the art bounds, not the artboard.
(unverified) A CMYK document is converted to RGB on export using the document colour settings; check colours on vivid CMYK art.

review.changes: summary no longer asserts "always RGB" (the card's own gotcha marks the CMYK-to-RGB conversion unverified); it now states only that the class has no colour-space or ppi member

cards.name: ExportOptionsPhotoshop
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsPhotoshop
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.PHOTOSHOP: rasterizes the document to a PSD at 72-2400 ppi in RGB, CMYK or greyscale, optionally keeping layers as Photoshop layers and text as editable type layers, one PSD per artboard if asked.
use_for: hand a layout to a Photoshop retoucher with layers intact
build a layered PSD base for a mockup or composite
rasterize vector art at print resolution in CMYK
avoid: keeping vectors editable: shapes become pixels; send the .ai or a PDF instead
web images: PSD is heavy; use ExportOptionsPNG24 or ExportOptionsJPEG
cards.how: new ExportOptionsPhotoshop(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.PHOTOSHOP, options).

key_members.name: imageColorSpace
key_members.use: ImageColorSpace of the PSD: RGB (default), CMYK, GrayScale ...

key_members.name: writeLayers
key_members.use: keep layers as PSD layers (default true); false flattens

key_members.name: editableText
key_members.use: export text as editable type layers (default true)

key_members.name: maximumEditability
key_members.use: keep as much layer/group structure as possible (default true)

key_members.name: warnings
key_members.use: show a dialog on setting conflicts (default true)

key_members.name: saveMultipleArtboards
key_members.use: write one PSD per artboard (default false)

key_members.name: artboardRange
key_members.use: artboards to export when saveMultipleArtboards is true; '' = all

gotchas: warnings defaults to true, and a conflict dialog stalls an unattended run; set it false and set app.userInteractionLevel = UserInteractionLevel.DONTDISPLAYALERTS.
resolution defaults to 150 ppi, not 300.
(unverified) Art whose appearance cannot be kept as separate PSD layers is merged into one raster layer; check the layer structure of the result.
(unverified) Only RGB, CMYK and GrayScale of the ImageColorSpace enum are meaningful for a PSD export.
(unverified) With saveMultipleArtboards the artboard name is appended to each file name.

review.changes: layer-merging behaviour gotcha is not in the harvest, so it is now marked unverified

cards.name: ExportOptionsPNG24
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsPNG24
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.PNG24, the legacy Save-for-Web style 24-bit PNG writer with full alpha transparency, matte colour, scale percentages that set the pixel size, anti-aliasing and artboard clipping.
use_for: transparent logos and icons for web and apps
UI assets and stickers with soft anti-aliased edges
lossless previews of flat vector art at 1x/2x/3x
avoid: photos and big backgrounds where file size matters: use ExportOptionsJPEG or ExportOptionsWebP
print rasters: use ExportOptionsTIFF or PDFSaveOptions
many artboards at several sizes: Document.exportForScreens with ExportForScreensOptionsPNG24 is simpler
cards.how: new ExportOptionsPNG24(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.PNG24, options).

key_members.name: matte
key_members.use: matte the artboard with matteColor (default true)

key_members.name: matteColor
key_members.use: RGBColor background used when transparency is off, white by default

key_members.name: verticalScale
key_members.use: percent of 72 ppi for the height

key_members.name: artBoardClipping
key_members.use: clip to the artboard instead of the art bounds (default false)

key_members.name: dimensions
key_members.use: Dimensions box (width/height) to contain the raster

key_members.name: saveAsHTML
key_members.use: also write an HTML file (keep false)

gotchas: Pixel size = points x horizontalScale/100 (72 ppi base); for @2x assets set both scales to 200.
artBoardClipping defaults to false (crop to the art bounds); set true to keep the full artboard including empty margins.
With transparency false, transparent areas are filled with matteColor (white unless you change it).
(unverified) How dimensions interacts with the scale percentages; test before relying on it.

cards.name: ExportOptionsPNG8
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsPNG8
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.PNG8: an indexed-colour PNG with a 2-256 colour palette, reduction, dither and web-snap controls, on/off transparency, interlacing, matte and scale percentages; the smallest PNGs for flat art.
use_for: flat icons and diagrams for the web at tiny file size
limited-palette retro or pixel-style graphics
email graphics with a handful of colours
avoid: gradients, shadows and photos: banding; use ExportOptionsPNG24
soft transparent edges over varying backgrounds: fringing against matteColor; use ExportOptionsPNG24
cards.how: new ExportOptionsPNG8(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.PNG8, options).

key_members.name: colorDither
key_members.use: ColorDitherMethod; NOREDUCTION gives clean flat fills

key_members.name: webSnap
key_members.use: 0-100 snap of palette colours to the web palette

key_members.name: matte
key_members.use: blend edge pixels with matteColor (default true)

key_members.name: matteColor
key_members.use: RGBColor for matting, white by default

key_members.name: verticalScale
key_members.use: percent of 72 ppi for the height

gotchas: Transparency is binary: anti-aliased edges are blended with matteColor, so set it to the destination background colour.
Unlike ExportOptionsGIF there is no lossy (infoLossPercent) setting.
artBoardClipping defaults to false and the pixel size comes from the scale percentages (72 ppi base).
The default colorDither DIFFUSION adds noise to flat fills; use NOREDUCTION for icons.

cards.name: ExportOptionsSVG
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsSVG
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.SVG, the classic Save-As-SVG writer: DTD/profile, font handling (SVG fonts or outlines) and glyph subsetting, linked or embedded images, coordinate precision, text encoding, CSS placement, optional SVGZ compression and Illustrator round-trip data.
use_for: SVG for vector interchange where Illustrator editability must survive
SVG Tiny or Basic profiles for devices that require them
one SVG per artboard from a multi-artboard file
avoid: lean web and UI icons: output is verbose; use ExportOptionsWebOptimizedSVG (ExportType.WOSVG)
text that must look identical in every browser: SVG fonts are not rendered by most browsers; set fontType to OUTLINEFONT
cards.how: new ExportOptionsSVG(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.SVG, options).

key_members.name: fontSubsetting
key_members.use: which glyphs to embed: None ... ALLGLYPHS (default)

key_members.name: embedRasterImages
key_members.use: embed placed images (default false = link to files)

key_members.name: preserveEditability
key_members.use: add Illustrator private data for round-trips (default false)

key_members.name: optimizeForSVGViewer
key_members.use: optimize for the Adobe SVG Viewer

key_members.name: artboardRange
key_members.use: artboards to write when saveMultipleArtboards is true; '' = all

gotchas: fontType defaults to SVGFONT, which browsers do not render; use OUTLINEFONT for faithful text (it then stops being selectable text).
embedRasterImages defaults to false, so placed images are linked rather than embedded and the SVG is not self-contained; set it true for a single-file delivery.
preserveEditability adds Illustrator private data and can multiply the file size; leave it false for delivery.
documentEncoding defaults to ASCII; use UTF8 for non-Latin text such as Devanagari.
compressed true writes gzip data; name the file .svgz.
Member names keep the dictionary's casing: sVGAutoKerning, sVGTextOnPath, DTD.

review.changes: embedRasterImages gotcha no longer claims images are written as separate files next to the SVG (not in the harvest); it now says they are linked, not embedded

cards.name: ExportOptionsTIFF
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsTIFF
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.TIFF: rasterizes the artwork to a TIFF at 72-2400 ppi in RGB, CMYK or greyscale with art- or type-optimized anti-aliasing, optional LZW compression, PC/Mac byte order and ICC profile, optionally one file per artboard.
use_for: print-ready rasters of vector art at 300 ppi CMYK
high-resolution rasters for prepress or older RIPs
large rasters beyond the scale limits of the JPEG/PNG classes
avoid: web delivery: files are large; use ExportOptionsPNG24, ExportOptionsJPEG or ExportOptionsWebP
keeping vectors: use PDFSaveOptions or EPSSaveOptions
cards.how: new ExportOptionsTIFF(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.TIFF, options).

key_members.name: saveMultipleArtboards
key_members.use: export the artboards given by artboardRange, one TIFF each (default false)

key_members.name: artboardRange
key_members.use: artboards to export when saveMultipleArtboards is true; '' = all

gotchas: The member is spelled lZWCompression (lower-case l, then ZW); a differently cased name is a different property and changes nothing.
antiAliasing here is an AntiAliasingMethod enum, not a bool as in the JPEG/PNG classes.
resolution defaults to 150 ppi; set 300 for print.
(unverified) With saveMultipleArtboards false the image covers the artwork bounds rather than the artboard; set it true with artboardRange '1' to get exact artboard size.
(unverified) There is no transparency option; empty areas come out white.

review.changes: saveMultipleArtboards key member no longer asserts the art-bounds behaviour that the card's own gotcha marks unverified; added its harvested default false

cards.name: ExportOptionsWebOptimizedSVG
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsWebOptimizedSVG
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.WOSVG, the modern Export-As-SVG writer: lean markup with optional minify, responsive sizing, ID naming style, CSS placement, font handling, coordinate precision and embed/link choice for images, optionally one file per artboard.
use_for: web and app icons and illustrations
inline SVG for websites
icon sets exported one artboard per file
avoid: round-tripping back into Illustrator with every feature: use ExportOptionsSVG with preserveEditability
deliveries that need a specific DTD such as SVG Tiny: use ExportOptionsSVG
cards.how: new ExportOptionsWebOptimizedSVG(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.WOSVG, options).

key_members.name: svgId
key_members.use: SVGIdType: SVGIDREGULAR (default, layer names), SVGIDUNIQUE, SVGIDMINIMAL

key_members.name: svgMinify
key_members.use: strip whitespace and shorten markup (default false)

key_members.name: svgResponsive
key_members.use: drop fixed width/height so the SVG scales to its container (default true)

gotchas: svgResponsive defaults to true, so width/height attributes are dropped and the SVG stretches to its container; set false for fixed-size icons.
svgId SVGIDREGULAR uses layer/object names as ids; when several SVGs are inlined on one page use SVGIDUNIQUE to avoid id clashes.
rasterImageLocation PRESERVE keeps the document's link/embed state; set EMBED for a self-contained file.
fontType SVGFONT is not rendered by most browsers; OUTLINEFONT converts text to paths.

cards.name: ExportOptionsWebP
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ExportOptionsWebP
cards.summary: Option set for exportFile with ExportType.WEBP: writes a WebP raster, lossless by default or lossy with imageQuality 0-100, with optional alpha, ICC profile, XMP metadata, an anti-aliasing mode and a PPI that sets the pixel size.
use_for: lightweight web images and banners rendered from vector art
transparent WebP stickers and UI assets
page-speed friendly replacements for PNG24 exports
avoid: destinations that refuse WebP (some print vendors, older email clients): use ExportOptionsPNG24 or ExportOptionsJPEG
exporting many artboards at several sizes: Document.exportForScreens with ExportForScreensOptionsWebP
cards.how: new ExportOptionsWebP(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.exportFile(file, ExportType.WEBP, options).

key_members.name: losslessCompression
key_members.use: true (default) = lossless; set false so imageQuality applies

key_members.name: PPI
key_members.use: output resolution, default 72; sets the pixel size

key_members.name: matteColor
key_members.use: RGBColor background used when isTransparent is false

gotchas: imageQuality is ignored while losslessCompression is true (the default).
Pixel size comes from PPI (default 72); there are no scale percentages as in the legacy PNG/JPEG classes.
Do not confuse it with ExportForScreensOptionsWebP, the option class for Document.exportForScreens, which also has scaleType/scaleTypeValue.
(unverified) Whether the export is cropped to the active artboard or to the artwork bounds.

cards.name: ImageCaptureOptions
cards.path: File export options classes for Adobe Illustrator/ImageCaptureOptions
cards.summary: Options for Document.imageCapture(file, clipBounds, options), which renders the artwork inside a rectangle to a 24-bit PNG at 72-2400 ppi, with optional transparency, matte and anti-aliasing.
use_for: quick PNG crops of a region for thumbnails, contact sheets or QC frames
a PNG of one object by passing its visibleBounds as the clip rectangle
automated preview images for a review step
avoid: deliverable exports with full options: use exportFile with ExportOptionsPNG24, or exportForScreens
other formats: imageCapture only writes PNG
cards.how: new ImageCaptureOptions(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.imageCapture(file, clipBounds, options). clipBounds is an optional [left, top, right, bottom] rectangle; the dictionary says that when it is omitted the whole artwork bounds are captured.

key_members.name: matteColor
key_members.use: RGBColor for the matte, white by default

gotchas: antiAliasing and transparency both default to false: without setting antiAliasing the PNG has jagged edges.
clipBounds is a 4-number array with top greater than bottom (Illustrator's y axis points up); an item's visibleBounds or an artboard's artboardRect can be passed as is.
Default resolution is 150 ppi.
(unverified) The capture renders all visible art inside the rectangle, including other objects that overlap it.

review.changes: how: clipBounds is optional per the harvested imageCapture signature (omitted = whole artwork bounds); dropped the unverified "in document coordinates" claim

cards.name: OpenOptions
cards.path: File opening options classes for Adobe Illustrator/OpenOptions
cards.summary: Options for app.open(file, documentColorSpace, options) on Illustrator documents: whether legacy text is updated, whether spot colours in legacy gradient meshes are kept, how pre-CS4 artboards, crop areas and print tiles become artboards, whether the file opens as a library (swatches, brushes, graphic styles, symbols), and whether it is added to Recent Files.
use_for: batch-opening old .ai/.eps archives without legacy-text prompts
loading a swatch, brush or symbol library from an .ai file by script
headless batch runs that should not fill the Recent Files list
avoid: PDF, PSD or DWG import settings: those live in app.preferences.PDFFileOptions, photoshopFileOptions and AutoCADFileOptions (OpenOptionsPDF, OpenOptionsPhotoshop, OpenOptionsAutoCAD)
cards.how: new OpenOptions(), set properties, pass as the third argument of app.open(file, documentColorSpace, options).

key_members.name: updateLegacyText
key_members.use: convert pre-Illustrator-11 text to editable text (default false)

key_members.name: updateLegacyGradientMesh
key_members.use: keep spot colours in pre-CS3 gradient meshes (default true)

key_members.name: openAs
key_members.use: LibraryType: ILLUSTRATORARTWORK (default), SWATCHES, BRUSHES, GRAPHICSTYLES, SYMBOLS

key_members.name: convertCropAreaToArtboard
key_members.use: turn pre-CS4 crop areas into artboards (default true)

key_members.name: createArtboardWithArtworkBoundingBox
key_members.use: make the artboard fit the art (default false)

key_members.name: convertTilesToArtboard
key_members.use: turn print tiles into artboards (default false)

key_members.name: addToRecentFiles
key_members.use: list the file in Recent Files (default true)

gotchas: updateLegacyText defaults to false, so old text stays as non-editable legacy text; setting it true converts the text and can reflow lines, so check layouts.
Opening old or foreign files can still raise dialogs (missing fonts, colour profile mismatch); set app.userInteractionLevel = UserInteractionLevel.DONTDISPLAYALERTS for unattended runs.
addToRecentFiles defaults to true; set false in batch jobs.
documentColorSpace (the second app.open argument) only applies to documents saved with multiple colour models (pre-Illustrator 9), per the dictionary; pass it only for such files.

review.changes: summary: updateLegacyGradientMesh keeps spot colours in legacy meshes (per its harvested description), it does not "update" meshes; removed PS equivalent OpenOptions (an abstract base class with no members in the PS harvest, so it cannot do this job); documentColorSpace gotcha now uses the harvested parameter description instead of an unverified guess

cards.name: OpenOptionsAutoCAD
cards.path: File opening options classes for Adobe Illustrator/OpenOptionsAutoCAD
cards.summary: The AutoCAD (DWG/DXF) import settings Illustrator uses when opening or placing a CAD drawing: which layout, scale mode (original size, fit artboard or by value), percent scale, unit mapping and ratio, centring, layer merging and lineweight scaling.
use_for: importing architectural or engineering plans at a known scale
turning DWG/DXF line work into editable vector art for signage or diagrams
batch conversion of CAD drawings with consistent units
avoid: exporting to CAD: that is ExportType.AUTOCAD with its own export option class
raster plans (scans): place them as images instead
cards.how: Not constructed with new: it is the live preferences object app.preferences.AutoCADFileOptions (its members are instance-scope, with parent/typename). Set its properties, then app.open(file) or place the drawing.

key_members.name: unit
key_members.use: AutoCADUnit the drawing units map to (default Millimeters)

key_members.name: selectedLayoutName
key_members.use: name of the drawing layout to import

key_members.name: centerArtwork
key_members.use: centre the art on the artboard (default true)

key_members.name: mergeLayers
key_members.use: merge CAD layers into one (default false)

key_members.name: scaleLineweights
key_members.use: scale line weights with the drawing (default false)

key_members.name: parent
key_members.use: the Preferences object it belongs to

gotchas: These are application-wide preferences: values persist for later opens and places in the session; restore them after the job.
The default FitArtboard scaling loses real-world scale; use OriginalSize or ScaleByValue with unit and unitScaleRatio for measured drawings.
scaleLineweights defaults to false, so lines keep their absolute weight when a big drawing is scaled down and plans look heavy.
(unverified) What happens when selectedLayoutName does not match a layout in the drawing.

cards.name: OpenOptionsPDF
cards.path: File opening options classes for Adobe Illustrator/OpenOptionsPDF
cards.summary: The PDF import settings Illustrator applies when opening or placing a PDF: which page or page range, which PDF box defines the crop, and whether placed pages come in as links.
use_for: opening page N of a supplier PDF as editable artwork
placing a PDF trimmed to its trim or art box (no bleed/slug)
batch-converting PDF pages to Illustrator files
avoid: keeping a PDF pixel-identical: opening converts it to editable art with font substitution; place it linked instead
cards.how: Reached as app.preferences.PDFFileOptions, a live preferences object (instance-scope members with parent/typename), not created with new. Set it before app.open(pdfFile) or before placing a PDF.

key_members.name: pageToOpen
key_members.use: page used when opening a multipage PDF (default 1)

key_members.name: pDFCropToBox
key_members.use: PDFBoxType for placing: PDFMEDIABOX (default), PDFTRIMBOX, PDFARTBOX, PDFCROPBOX, PDFBLEEDBOX, PDFBOUNDINGBOX

key_members.name: placeAsLinks
key_members.use: import pages as links (default true when the range is 'all')

key_members.name: parent
key_members.use: the Preferences object it belongs to

gotchas: The property name is pDFCropToBox with the dictionary's odd casing.
These are global preferences: a page number set by one script stays in effect for later opens and places; reset pageToOpen to 1 afterwards.
Opening (not placing) converts the page to editable Illustrator art: missing fonts are substituted and text can split into many small objects.
(unverified) pDFCropToBox affects placing only; opening uses the page's own boxes.

cards.name: OpenOptionsPhotoshop
cards.path: File opening options classes for Adobe Illustrator/OpenOptionsPhotoshop
cards.summary: The PSD import settings Illustrator applies when opening or placing a Photoshop file: convert layers to objects or flatten, keep image maps, slices and hidden layers, and choose a layer comp.
use_for: bringing a layered PSD into Illustrator with layers as separate objects
importing a specific layer comp of a mockup PSD
batch-converting PSD comps into Illustrator layouts
avoid: keeping the PSD live-editable in Photoshop: place it linked instead of opening/embedding
cards.how: Reached as app.preferences.photoshopFileOptions (lower-case p), a live preferences object, not created with new. Set it before app.open(psdFile) or before placing/embedding a PSD.

key_members.name: preserveLayers
key_members.use: convert layers to objects (default true); false flattens to one image

key_members.name: layerComp
key_members.use: name of the layer comp to use

key_members.name: parent
key_members.use: the Preferences object it belongs to

gotchas: Note the casing: app.preferences.photoshopFileOptions, while PDFFileOptions and AutoCADFileOptions start upper-case.
These are global preferences that persist for later opens and places in the session; reset them after the job.
preserveHiddenLayers defaults to false, so hidden layers are dropped.
(unverified) A PSD placed as a link always shows as one flattened image; the layer options apply when opening or embedding.

cards.name: EPSSaveOptions
cards.path: File save options classes for Adobe Illustrator/EPSSaveOptions
cards.summary: Options for Document.saveAs(file, options) as Illustrator EPS: version compatibility, preview type, font embedding, inclusion of linked images, CMYK PostScript, PostScript level 2/3, transparency flattening for old versions, overprint handling and one file per artboard.
use_for: print and sign vendors that still require EPS
stock vector submissions that ask for EPS10 (Compatibility.ILLUSTRATOR10)
logo packages with an EPS version
avoid: modern print workflows: EPS cannot keep live transparency or layers; use PDFSaveOptions (PDF/X-4)
web output: use ExportOptionsWebOptimizedSVG
cards.how: new EPSSaveOptions(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.saveAs(file, options).

key_members.name: compatibility
key_members.use: Compatibility version, default ILLUSTRATOR24; ILLUSTRATOR10 = EPS10

key_members.name: flattenOutput
key_members.use: OutputFlattening for pre-version-9 targets: PRESERVEAPPEARANCE or PRESERVEPATHS

key_members.name: artboardRange
key_members.use: artboards to save when saveMultipleArtboards is true; '' = all

gotchas: saveAs re-targets the open document to the new file: a later doc.save() writes this format, not the .ai. Save the master first, or close with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES and reopen it.
embedAllFonts defaults to false; set it true before sending to a printer or stock site.
embedLinkedFiles defaults to false, so placed images stay as external links the recipient may not have.
flattenOutput only applies to pre-version-9 compatibility; the EPS PostScript itself always carries a flattened version of transparency.
(unverified) With saveMultipleArtboards the artboard name is appended to each file name.

cards.name: FXGSaveOptions
cards.path: File save options classes for Adobe Illustrator/FXGSaveOptions
cards.summary: Options for Document.saveAs(file, options) as FXG (Flash XML Graphics 1.0/2.0, the Flex and Flash Catalyst vector format): artboard range, whether filters, text, gradients and blends stay editable or are converted, unused symbols, linked-image downsampling and XMP. FXG is a legacy format; this card was not tested on 2026.
use_for: legacy Flex or Flash Catalyst pipelines that still consume FXG
editable XML vector output for old Adobe toolchains
avoid: any current web or app delivery: use ExportOptionsWebOptimizedSVG
print: use PDFSaveOptions
cards.how: new FXGSaveOptions(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.saveAs(file, options) with a .fxg file.

key_members.name: includeUnusedSymbols
key_members.use: write symbols not used on the artboard (default false)

key_members.name: downsampleLinkedImages
key_members.use: downsample linked images to 72 ppi (default false)

gotchas: (unverified) FXG belongs to the Flash/Flex era; recent Illustrator versions may no longer offer it in Save As, so run a test saveAs with this class before building on it.
saveAs re-targets the open document to the new file: a later doc.save() writes this format, not the .ai. Save the master first, or close with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES and reopen it.
downsampleLinkedImages reduces linked images to 72 ppi, which is fine for screen and wrong for print.

cards.name: IllustratorSaveOptions
cards.path: File save options classes for Adobe Illustrator/IllustratorSaveOptions
cards.summary: Options for Document.saveAs(file, options) in native .ai format: version compatibility (Illustrator 3 up to the current ILLUSTRATOR24 format), PDF-compatible content, compression, font subsetting and used-glyph embedding, ICC profile, embedding of linked images and per-artboard saving.
use_for: saving working master files from a script
down-saving to an older Illustrator version for a vendor
packaging an .ai with embedded images for handoff
avoid: sending to non-Adobe apps: use PDFSaveOptions or EPSSaveOptions
web delivery: use the SVG export classes
cards.how: new IllustratorSaveOptions(), set properties, then app.activeDocument.saveAs(file, options) with a .ai file.

key_members.name: compatibility
key_members.use: Compatibility: ILLUSTRATOR24 (default, current format), ILLUSTRATOR17 (CC), ILLUSTRATOR16 (CS6) ...

key_members.name: pdfCompatible
key_members.use: store a PDF copy inside the .ai (default true)

key_members.name: embedICCProfile
key_members.use: embed the document ICC profile (default false)

key_members.name: fontSubsetThreshold
key_members.use: embed a font subset when less than this % of glyphs are used (default 100)

key_members.name: embedUsedGlyphs
key_members.use: save used font glyphs (version 24 or later)

key_members.name: artboardRange
key_members.use: artboards to save when saveMultipleArtboards is true

gotchas: pdfCompatible defaults to true and is what lets InDesign and other apps place the .ai; false gives smaller files that other apps cannot read.
Saving to an older compatibility can expand or drop newer features (variable-width strokes, newer effects); keep ILLUSTRATOR24 for masters.
saveAs to a new path re-targets the open document to that file.
embedLinkedFiles true makes the file self-contained but much larger.

cards.name: PDFSaveOptions
cards.path: File save options classes for Adobe Illustrator/PDFSaveOptions
cards.summary: Options for Document.saveAs(file, options) as Adobe PDF: a named preset and/or compatibility, PDF/X standard, image compression and downsampling for colour, grey and mono images, printer's marks and bleed, colour conversion and output intent, transparency flattening, Acrobat layers, security passwords and permissions, and the artboard range (one artboard = one page).
use_for: print-ready PDF/X files with bleed and crop marks
lightweight review PDFs with downsampled images and no editing data
multi-page brochure PDFs from several artboards
password-protected client proofs
avoid: raster deliverables: use ExportOptionsPNG24, ExportOptionsJPEG or ExportOptionsTIFF
keeping the open .ai as the working file: saveAs switches the document to the PDF (see gotchas)
cards.how: new PDFSaveOptions(), optionally set pDFPreset to a name from app.PDFPresetsList, override single properties, then app.activeDocument.saveAs(file, options).

key_members.name: pDFPreset
key_members.use: preset name from app.PDFPresetsList, e.g. '[High Quality Print]'

key_members.name: compatibility
key_members.use: PDFCompatibility ACROBAT4-8 (default ACROBAT5); ACROBAT4 flattens transparency

key_members.name: preserveEditability
key_members.use: embed the full .ai for re-editing (default true)

key_members.name: artboardRange
key_members.use: artboards to write as pages; '' = all

key_members.name: colorDownsamplingImageThreshold
key_members.use: only images above this ppi are downsampled (default 225)

key_members.name: pageInformation
key_members.use: print file name/date on the page

key_members.name: bleedOffsetRect
key_members.use: bleed on the four sides, in points

key_members.name: colorConversionID
key_members.use: ColorConversion policy: none, repurpose or convert to destination

key_members.name: outputIntentProfile
key_members.use: output intent profile name for PDF/X

gotchas: saveAs re-targets the open document to the new file: a later doc.save() writes this format, not the .ai. Save the master first, or close with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES and reopen it.
pDFPreset must be an exact name from app.PDFPresetsList, brackets included; (unverified) assign it first, because applying the preset can overwrite properties set before it.
preserveEditability defaults to true and embeds the whole .ai: big files that anyone can reopen and edit; set false for client and print delivery.
Downsampling does nothing while colorDownsamplingMethod is NODOWNSAMPLE (the default); colorDownsampling is the target ppi and colorDownsamplingImageThreshold the trigger.
(unverified) The order of the four bleedOffsetRect values is not clearly documented; set all four equal (8.504 pt = 3 mm).
documentPassword only takes effect when requireDocumentPassword is true (same for permissionPassword and requirePermissionPassword).
Member names keep the dictionary's casing: pDFPreset, pDFXStandard, pDFAllowPrinting.

cards.name: Point
cards.summary: A two-number coordinate (x/left, y/top) listed under Other Classes in the Illustrator 2026 dictionary (Photoshop lists the same class). In Illustrator it is the type of PageItem.position, of Document.windowCapture's windowSize and of Document.convertCoordinate's argument and result; in practice a plain [x, y] array is used wherever a point is expected.
use_for: reading and setting object positions ([x, y] in points)
converting between document and artboard coordinates
window capture sizes
avoid: rectangles and bounds: use 4-number arrays (see Rectangle)
cards.how: Behaves as a 2-element collection: p[0] is x, p[1] is y. Illustrator properties typed as Point (for example pageItem.position) take and return [x, y] arrays.

key_members.name: y
key_members.use: vertical coordinate in points (Illustrator: up is positive)

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: always 2: the class is a two-element collection

gotchas: Illustrator's scripting y axis points up: with the default artboard coordinate system (origin at the artboard's top-left), objects below the top edge have negative y, so subtract to move down.
app.coordinateSystem decides whether positions are artboard- or document-relative; Document.convertCoordinate translates a point between the two.
(unverified) Whether new Point(x, y) is available as a global constructor in Illustrator's engine; plain arrays always work.

review.changes: summary/how: dropped the "shared ExtendScript dictionary" and ScriptUI-location claims (the evidence is Illustrator omv.xml, Other Classes); named the harvested Point-typed members instead

cards.name: Rectangle
cards.summary: A four-number rectangle (left/x, top/y, right, bottom, plus width and height) listed under Other Classes in the Illustrator 2026 dictionary (Photoshop lists the same class). Illustrator's bounds (geometricBounds, visibleBounds, artboardRect, imageCapture and rasterize clipBounds) are typed Rect and use plain 4-number arrays [left, top, right, bottom].
use_for: reading artboard and object bounds to compute sizes and margins
building clip rectangles for imageCapture or rasterize
checking whether an object fits inside the artboard before export
avoid: drawing a rectangle shape: that is pathItems.rectangle(top, left, width, height), a different thing
cards.how: A 4-element collection: r[0] left, r[1] top, r[2] right, r[3] bottom. Illustrator DOM properties of type Rect take and return such arrays.

key_members.name: length
key_members.use: always 4: the class is a four-element collection

gotchas: In Illustrator arrays top is greater than bottom (y up), so height = top - bottom; (unverified) ScriptUI bounds are y-down (bottom > top).
Do not confuse with the rectangle shape method pathItems.rectangle(top, left, width, height), whose argument order starts with top.
(unverified) Whether new Rectangle() is available as a constructor in Illustrator's engine; arrays always work.

review.changes: summary no longer lists bleed rectangles as [l, t, r, b] (bleedOffsetRect order is unverified on the PDF and print-marks cards); dropped the unverified "ScriptUI bounds type" claim from summary, how and use_for; ScriptUI y-down note marked unverified

cards.name: Ink
cards.summary: One printing ink (a process ink or a spot colour) of a document, with its separation settings in inkInfo. Read the document's inks from doc.inkList; PrintColorSeparationOptions.inkList uses them to decide which plates print.
use_for: preflight: list the spot colours a print file will separate into
disable or convert an unwanted spot plate when printing separations
count inks against a job's colour budget
avoid: changing artwork colours: that is swatches and spot colours, not inks
PDF output: inks only steer Document.print separations
cards.how: Read-only source: app.activeDocument.inkList (an array of Ink). For printing, assign an (edited) ink array to PrintColorSeparationOptions.inkList. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: name
key_members.use: ink name (process ink or spot colour name)

key_members.name: inkInfo
key_members.use: InkInfo: print status, type, trapping, screen frequency and angle

gotchas: doc.inkList is built from the colours used in the artwork, so an unused spot swatch may not appear (unverified).
(unverified) Ink arrays come back as copies: edit the Ink objects, then assign the whole array to colorSeparationOptions.inkList.
Ink settings only matter for separated output (HOSTBASEDSEPARATION or INRIPSEPARATION), not composite prints.

cards.name: InkInfo
cards.summary: The separation settings of one Ink: whether it prints, is disabled or is converted to process (printingStatus), its type (cyan, magenta, yellow, black or custom), trapping type and order, neutral density, screen frequency and angle, dot shape and the custom ink's colour.
use_for: convert a stray spot colour to process at print time
set screen angle and frequency for a spot plate
set trapping order for press separations
avoid: changing the colour of the artwork: edit the spot swatch instead
cards.how: Reached as ink.inkInfo on an Ink from doc.inkList or PrintColorSeparationOptions.inkList. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: kind
key_members.use: InkType: CYANINK, MAGENTAINK, YELLOWINK, BLACKINK, CUSTOMINK

key_members.name: trappingOrder
key_members.use: order in which the ink traps, starting at 1

key_members.name: density
key_members.use: neutral density used for trapping decisions

key_members.name: customColor
key_members.use: the colour of a custom (spot) ink

gotchas: printingStatus CONVERTINK separates a spot ink into CMYK, the usual fix for an unwanted extra plate.
(unverified) frequency, angle and dotShape only affect host-based separations to a PostScript device.
customColor is only meaningful when kind is CUSTOMINK.

cards.name: Paper
cards.summary: A paper size an installed printer supports: its name plus a PaperInfo with width, height and imageable area. A printer's sizes are listed in PrinterInfo.paperSizes.
use_for: picking a valid paper name for an automated print job
checking that the sheet is big enough for artboard plus bleed and marks
avoid: setting the paper for a job: that is PrintPaperOptions.name (or its custom width/height)
cards.how: Read from app.printerList[i].printerInfo.paperSizes. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: name
key_members.use: paper size name as the driver reports it

key_members.name: paperInfo
key_members.use: PaperInfo: width, height, imageable area, custom flag

gotchas: Paper names are driver-specific; copy them from paperSizes instead of typing 'A4' or 'Letter'.
Sizes are in points (72 per inch, about 2.835 per mm).

cards.name: PaperInfo
cards.summary: Size data for one Paper: width and height in points, the printer's imageable area, and whether it is a custom size.
use_for: checking that a sheet fits the artboard plus bleed and printer's marks
finding the printable (imageable) area of a paper size
avoid: defining a custom sheet for a job: set PrintPaperOptions width/height instead
cards.how: Reached as paper.paperInfo on a Paper from PrinterInfo.paperSizes. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: customPaper
key_members.use: true for a custom paper size

gotchas: Units are points (72 per inch).
(unverified) The order of the four imageableArea values; read all four and compare with width/height.

cards.name: PPDFile
cards.summary: A PostScript Printer Description (PPD) file Illustrator knows about: its model name plus PPDInfo with the file path, PostScript level and available halftone screens. app.PPDFileList returns these.
use_for: choosing a PPD for PostScript printing or print-to-file
listing available device descriptions on a print workstation
avoid: non-PostScript printers: PPDs do not apply
cards.how: List with app.PPDFileList; set PrintOptions.PPDName to a name from it. For full details call app.getPPDFileInfo(name).

key_members.name: PPDInfo
key_members.use: PPDFileInfo: file path, language level, screens

gotchas: For speed, entries in app.PPDFileList only carry the model name and file path; call app.getPPDFileInfo(name) to get screens and language level.
PPDs only matter for PostScript output.
cards.example:
var list = app.PPDFileList;
for (var i = 0; i < list.length; i++) $.writeln(list[i].name);

cards.name: PPDFileInfo
cards.summary: Details of one PPD: PostScript language level, the .ppd file path, and the lists of halftone screens and screen spot functions the device offers.
use_for: picking a halftone screen for separations
checking a device's PostScript level before choosing print options
avoid: non-PostScript printers
cards.how: Get it with app.getPPDFileInfo(name), using a name from app.PPDFileList. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).
gotchas: The PPDInfo of an entry in app.PPDFileList is not filled in; use app.getPPDFileInfo(name).
languageLevel is a string, not a number.

cards.name: PrintColorManagementOptions
cards.summary: Colour-management settings for Document.print: the profile mode (source, printer, custom or old style), the rendering intent and the profile name.
use_for: proof prints with a specific printer ICC profile
consistent rendering intent across batch-printed proofs
avoid: colour conversion in PDF files: use PDFSaveOptions colorConversionID/colorDestinationID
cards.how: new PrintColorManagementOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.colorManagementOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).
gotchas: (unverified) name is used with CUSTOMPROFILE and must match an installed ICC profile's description.
(unverified) If both Illustrator and the printer driver manage colour the output is converted twice; turn colour management off in one of them.

cards.name: PrintColorSeparationOptions
cards.summary: Separation settings for Document.print: composite, host-based or in-RIP separations, converting all spot colours to process, overprinting black, and the per-ink list that decides which plates print.
use_for: printing separation proofs per plate
converting all spot colours to CMYK at print time
overprinting black text on press proofs
avoid: PDF separations previews: use Acrobat Output Preview on a PDF instead
cards.how: new PrintColorSeparationOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.colorSeparationOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: convertSpotColors
key_members.use: convert every spot colour to process (default false)

key_members.name: inkList
key_members.use: array of Ink with per-plate settings

gotchas: Separations need a PostScript device; INRIPSEPARATION also needs in-RIP support (check PrinterInfo.inRIPSeparationSupport).
The default COMPOSITE prints all colours on one sheet and ignores the ink list.
(unverified) inkList returns copies; edit the inks and assign the whole array back.

cards.name: PrintCoordinateOptions
cards.summary: Placement settings for Document.print: orientation, emulsion flip, position on the sheet (nine anchors), fit to page, horizontal and vertical scale (1-10000%) and tiling of oversize art across sheets.
use_for: fit-to-page proofs of large posters
tiled prints of banners on office printers
mirrored output for film or transfers
avoid: resizing the artwork itself: scale the art or artboard instead
cards.how: new PrintCoordinateOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.coordinateOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: fitToPage
key_members.use: scale proportionally to fit the page (default false)

gotchas: (unverified) fitToPage overrides horizontalScale/verticalScale.
emulsion true mirrors the print; it is for film output, never for normal proofs.
Tiling only kicks in when the art is larger than the sheet.

cards.name: Printer
cards.summary: An installed system printer as Illustrator sees it: its name plus a PrinterInfo with type, PostScript level, colour support, resolutions and paper sizes. app.printerList returns them.
use_for: choosing the target printer in an automated print job
checking a printer's capabilities before setting separation or PostScript options
avoid: setting the printer: that is PrintOptions.printerName
cards.how: List with app.printerList; copy a name into PrintOptions.printerName. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: name
key_members.use: printer name, as PrintOptions.printerName expects it

gotchas: PrintOptions.printerName must match Printer.name exactly; take it from app.printerList instead of typing it.
Virtual printers such as PDF writers are listed too.
(unverified) Offline printers still appear in the list.

cards.name: PrinterInfo
cards.summary: Capabilities of one printer: PostScript or not and its level, colour, greyscale or black-and-white, default and maximum resolution, in-RIP separation and binary printing support, supported paper sizes and custom paper limits.
use_for: deciding whether separations or PostScript options can be used
checking custom paper limits for banners
listing paper sizes for a printer
avoid: changing printer behaviour: these are capabilities; settings go on PrintOptions and its sub-options
cards.how: Reached as printer.printerInfo on an entry of app.printerList. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).
gotchas: Separation and PostScript options only work when printerType is POSTSCRIPTPRINTER.
(unverified) The dictionary marks the members writable but they describe the device; treat them as read-only.
(unverified) Custom paper limits are in points, like PrintPaperOptions width/height; the dictionary gives no unit.

review.changes: unit of the custom paper limits is not in the harvest: gotcha marked unverified

cards.name: PrintFlattenerOptions
cards.summary: Transparency flattening settings used when printing (PrintOptions.flattenerOptions) and for flattened PDFs (PDFSaveOptions.flattenerOptions): raster/vector balance 0-100, rasterization and gradient/mesh resolution, text and strokes to outlines, clipping complex regions and overprint handling.
use_for: PostScript printing of artwork with transparency, shadows and blend modes
PDF/X-1a or Acrobat 4 PDFs where transparency must be flattened
fixing stitching or thin-text problems at the flattening stage
avoid: modern PDF output (Acrobat 5+ without PDF/X-1a): transparency stays live and these settings do nothing
cards.how: new PrintFlattenerOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.flattenerOptions or PDFSaveOptions.flattenerOptions.

key_members.name: flatteningBalance
key_members.use: 0 = rasterize all transparency, 100 (default) = keep max vectors

key_members.name: gradientResolution
key_members.use: ppi for gradients and meshes, 1-9600, default 300

key_members.name: clipComplexRegions
key_members.use: clip boundaries between raster and vector areas to paths (default false)

gotchas: Flattening only happens when transparency cannot travel: PostScript printing, ACROBAT4 compatibility or PDF/X-1a/X-3.
A named preset (flattenerPreset on PrintOptions or PDFSaveOptions, names from app.flattenerPresetsList) is simpler; (unverified) which wins when both are set.
convertTextToOutlines keeps text widths consistent where only part of the text is flattened, but removes live fonts.
clipComplexRegions reduces visible stitching where raster and vector areas meet.

review.changes: overprint key member said "preserve or simulate"; the harvested PDFOverprint enum is PRESERVEPDFOVERPRINT / DISCARDPDFOVERPRINT (no simulate), default PRESERVEPDFOVERPRINT

cards.name: PrintFontOptions
cards.summary: Font handling for PostScript printing: download no fonts, subsets or complete fonts to the device, and the substitution policy for missing fonts (oblique, tint or device fonts).
use_for: reliable text on PostScript printers and print-to-file
reducing PostScript size by downloading font subsets
avoid: non-PostScript printers: the driver handles fonts
PDF output: font embedding is set on PDFSaveOptions (fontSubsetThreshold)
cards.how: new PrintFontOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.fontOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).
gotchas: Only PostScript output uses these settings.
(unverified) DOWNLOADNONE relies on fonts resident in the printer; missing ones are substituted (often Courier).

cards.name: PrintJobOptions
cards.summary: Job-level print settings: which layers print, the print bounds (artboard, artwork or crop), copies, collate, reverse order, print to a file, print as bitmap at a resolution, job name, and all artboards or a range.
use_for: printing a range of artboards in a batch
printing to a PostScript file for a RIP
proof prints of all layers including non-printing ones
avoid: saving a PDF: use PDFSaveOptions with saveAs
cards.how: new PrintJobOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.jobOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: file
key_members.use: File to print to instead of the device

key_members.name: artboardRange
key_members.use: range such as '1-3' when printAllArtboards is false

gotchas: artboardRange is ignored unless printAllArtboards is set to false.
The default designation VISIBLEPRINTABLELAYERS skips layers marked non-printing, such as template layers.
(unverified) Printing to a file writes PostScript and needs a PostScript printer or PPD selected.
printAsBitmap is a last-resort workaround for PostScript errors; it rasterizes the whole page.

cards.name: PrintOptions
cards.summary: The container passed to Document.print(options): printer, PPD, print preset and flattener preset names, plus the sub-option objects for paper, job, separations, placement, marks, fonts, PostScript, colour management and flattening.
use_for: unattended printing of proofs from a script
applying a saved print preset to many documents
printing separations or PostScript files for a RIP
avoid: PDF output: use PDFSaveOptions with saveAs
cards.how: var po = new PrintOptions(); set the name properties, create and attach sub-option objects (new PrintJobOptions() etc.), then app.activeDocument.print(po).
gotchas: Sub-options are separate objects: create each with new, set it, then assign it to the PrintOptions property.
printerName must match a name in app.printerList exactly, and printPreset a name in app.printPresetsList.
(unverified) Which wins when printPreset and explicit sub-options disagree; set one or the other.
Printing blocks Illustrator until the job is spooled; set app.userInteractionLevel = UserInteractionLevel.DONTDISPLAYALERTS so no dialog waits for a click.

cards.name: PrintPageMarksOptions
cards.summary: Printer's marks for Document.print: trim marks and their weight, registration marks, colour bars, page information, Roman or Japanese mark style, and the bleed and marks offset rectangles.
use_for: press proofs with crop marks and colour bars
printing with bleed on oversize sheets for hand trimming
avoid: marks in a PDF file: use PDFSaveOptions trimMarks/registrationMarks/colorBars
cards.how: new PrintPageMarksOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.pageMarksOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: trimMarksWeight
key_members.use: trim mark stroke weight in points (default 0.125)

key_members.name: bleedOffsetRect
key_members.use: bleed on each side, in points

key_members.name: marksOffsetRect
key_members.use: distance of the marks from the trim, in points

gotchas: Marks and bleed need a sheet larger than the artboard; on a same-size sheet they fall off the page.
(unverified) The order of the four values in bleedOffsetRect and marksOffsetRect; set all four equal.
Japanese style draws double (tombo) crop marks.

cards.name: PrintPaperOptions
cards.summary: Paper choice for Document.print: a named paper size of the selected printer, or a custom width, height and offset in points, with optional transverse (rotated 90 degrees) feed.
use_for: choosing A3/tabloid sheets for proofs with marks
custom roll or banner sizes on large-format printers
avoid: changing the artboard size: edit the artboard instead
cards.how: new PrintPaperOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.paperOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: name
key_members.use: paper name from the printer's PrinterInfo.paperSizes

key_members.name: transverse
key_members.use: rotate the art 90 degrees on custom paper

gotchas: name must match a Paper.name of the selected printer exactly.
Custom width/height only work when PrinterInfo.customPaperSupport is true and within its min/max limits.
Units are points.

review.changes: width key member no longer invents "0 = use the named size"; states the harvested default 0

cards.name: PrintPostScriptOptions
cards.summary: PostScript output settings for Document.print: language level 1-3, binary or ASCII data, negative printing, image compression (none, RLE or JPEG), forced continuous tone, level-1 compatible gradient and mesh printing, and shading resolution.
use_for: printing to PostScript RIPs and imagesetters
writing PostScript files for older devices
fixing gradient banding or errors on old printers
avoid: non-PostScript printers: these settings are ignored
cards.how: new PrintPostScriptOptions(), set it, assign to PrintOptions.postScriptOptions. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: binaryPrinting
key_members.use: send binary instead of ASCII data

key_members.name: compatibleShading
key_members.use: level-1 compatible gradient and mesh printing

gotchas: negativePrinting inverts the image (for film); never use it for paper proofs.
binaryPrinting is faster but some spoolers cannot pass binary data; check PrinterInfo.binaryPrintingSupport.
JPEG imageCompression is lossy.

cards.name: Screen
cards.summary: One halftone screen a PPD offers (a named frequency/resolution combination): its name plus ScreenInfo with frequency, angle and whether it is the default.
use_for: choosing screening for host-based separations on a PostScript device
avoid: composite or non-PostScript printing: screens are not used
cards.how: Read from app.getPPDFileInfo(name).screenList. Part of the print API: build a PrintOptions, attach the sub-option objects, and call app.activeDocument.print(options).

key_members.name: name
key_members.use: screen name, e.g. a lpi / dpi combination

gotchas: The list is only filled in through app.getPPDFileInfo(name), not on entries of app.PPDFileList.
Screens only matter for separations on PostScript devices.
